High-level goals and objectives for Cotomata:

- Produce a robust, well-documented benchmark/dataset of code-editing and instruction-generation tasks for evaluating agent/LM behavior.
- Define and maintain clear, unambiguous feature specifications and canonical post-processing rules so evaluations are reproducible and comparable.
- Build reliable, reproducible test and CI infrastructure (environment setup, patch application, version management) to validate changes and prevent regressions.
- Ensure stable, well-defined integration points with language models and agent tooling while avoiding implicit mutation of LM input/output contracts.
- Improve developer experience and project maintainability through clear repository organization, automated checks, and up-to-date documentation.
- Promote transparency and adoption by preparing the benchmark for publication and community use (licensing, examples, and usage guides).

- Ensure optional external integrations (observers, third‑party services) degrade gracefully or can be feature‑gated so missing or misconfigured services do not crash or block core functionality.
- Build robust background processing with predictable backpressure: non‑blocking handlers, bounded/coalescing semantics, and throttling strategies so the system handles bursts stably.
- Enforce predictable resource and lifecycle management to avoid memory/CPU leaks and fragile long‑running behavior.
- Improve observability and diagnostics through structured logs, lightweight metrics, and actionable traces to accelerate troubleshooting and root‑cause analysis.
- Prevent environment‑ and dependency‑specific regressions via reproducible dependency management, targeted tests, and CI checks.
- Favor small, incremental, reviewable changes that unblock teammates quickly while minimizing regression risk and preserving system stability.
- Provide concise developer documentation and onboarding guidance that explains common failure modes, local testing workflows, and recommended practices.
- Maintain a modular, maintainable architecture that supports reproducible experiments, data/benchmark collection, and evolution of the prototype into a reusable background‑agent framework.
